name: OpenTTS
description: Unified HTTP TTS server (synesthesiam/opentts) fronting many open-source engines (espeak, flite, festival, nanotts, MaryTTS, and others) behind one REST/Swagger API and web UI on port 5500. Quart/Hypercorn ASGI, no authentication, archived read-only Oct 2025. Server-rendered index makes it partially Shodan http.html-visible.
auth_notes: No authentication on any endpoint. OpenTTS is a Quart (async) app behind the Hypercorn ASGI server; every route (/api/tts, /api/voices, /api/languages, /openapi, MaryTTS-compat /process) is public. Default port 5500. No API key, token, or basic auth documented. The project is archived read-only (Oct 6, 2025) so no security patches will be issued.

shodan_dorks.query: port:5500 http.html:"Unifies access to multiple open source text to speech"
shodan_dorks.rationale: The server-rendered index.html contains this exact description string in the body; direct high-signal match on the canonical port.
OpenTTS serves Swagger at /openapi/ and references it from the index; the openapi marker on port 5500 with the hypercorn stack catches instances whose title string varies by build.
Conjunctive: the OpenTTS name in the rendered index plus the voices reference (from /api/voices UI wiring) isolates OpenTTS from other Quart/Hypercorn TTS servers on 5500.
The multi-voice SSML capability description is present in the index body; pair with an /api/voices read (returns tts_name per voice) to scope engine set and build.

response_body_contains: Unifies access to multiple open source text to speech

known_vulns: No authentication - unauthenticated synthesis via /api/tts and full voice enumeration via /api/voices
Archived read-only Oct 2025 - no patches will ever be issued for any future finding
Multi-engine subprocess backends (espeak, flite, festival, nanotts, MaryTTS) - broad input/command surface depending on per-engine wrapping; SSML processor is an unaudited parser surface
/openapi/ Swagger UI publicly documents the entire API unauthenticated, aiding automated enumeration
MaryTTS-compatible /process endpoint makes it a drop-in for Home Assistant integrations that may leave it internet-exposed
risk_notes: Vectors on an exposed instance: (1) Unauthenticated synthesis / compute theft via /api/tts across whichever engines are installed; (2) Full metadata read via /api/voices - returns rich JSON per voice (id, name, gender, language, locale, tts_name), a clean unauth enumeration of the deployment's engine and voice inventory; (3) Multi-engine subprocess surface - OpenTTS shells out to espeak/flite/festival/nanotts/MaryTTS, so the SSML and text input path is a broad, per-engine-dependent injection/parser surface worth verifying; (4) Archived project - any issue found is permanent, no upstream fix. OpenTTS is partially Shodan http.html-visible: the index is server-rendered (Jinja, not a pure SPA) and carries the 'Unifies access to multiple open source text to speech systems' description and OpenTTS name in the body, so a body-string dork harvests it. Server header is 'hypercorn-h11' - identical to Mimic3, so disambiguate by port (5500 vs 59125) and the index strings.
deployment_notes: Quart async app behind Hypercorn ASGI on port 5500 (--port default 5500). Distributed as per-language Docker images synesthesiam/opentts:<LANG> on Docker Hub (tags en, de, fr, es, ja, zh, and ~20 more), each bundling the voices for that language. Server header is 'hypercorn-h11'. The index renders server-side so the OpenTTS name and description are in http.html; the /openapi/ Swagger UI and /api/voices JSON are the confirmation reads. Shares the Quart/Hypercorn stack (and thus the Server header) with Mimic3 - distinguish on port and body strings. Archived read-only Oct 6, 2025 (~1.1k stars, MIT). Commonly deployed as a Home Assistant TTS backend via the MaryTTS-compatible /process route, which is how some instances end up internet-reachable.
